compute.reported_as: For our benchmark simulations on the 8 x 8 lattice, we found that tau^{t,max}_{j<=2} = 16 and tau^{t,max}_{j>2} = 8, and jmax = 4 yield good accuracies while minimizing the number of variational parameters. We benchmark our method on the 8 x 8 lattice with PBC (...) The numerical values for the energies, details on the optimization procedure and hyperparameters can be found in Appendices A and B. || (...) a Markov Chain Monte Carlo algorithm with nearest neighbour exchange from which we take N_samples = 1024. We use a learning rate of eta = 0.005. For every run, we let the algorithm update the variational parameters 1000 times. Here, we consider the hidden dimension tau_j^t to be homogeneous for all layers and all angular momenta, and denote it with tau. || We use 4096 samples to estimate the expectation values in each step. Automatic differentiation [34] via the Jax library backpropagates the gradients through our network, and we use the Adam optimizer with learning rate 0.001. Furthermore, we use gradient clipping with a maximum gradient norm of 0.001. (...) we first carry out a Stochastic Reconfiguration (SR) step with a uniform diagonal shift of magnitude 0.01, followed by a step using the resulting update direction with an Adam optimizer. To save computational resources, in this optimization regime we use 256 samples and learning rate 0.005. Afterwards, we switch to the standard optimization strategy (and drop the SR step). || The software for this work was built on the NetKet library [21]. The computational resources (Stevin Supercomputer Infrastructure) and services used in this work were provided by the VSC (Flemish Supercomputer Center), and the Flemish Government - department EWI.

compute.reported_as: Appendix A (arXiv:2005.14142): The number of complex variational parameters in the RBM part is N_hidden for b_k and N_hidden × N_site for W_ik, respectively. As for the real variational parameters f_ij in the PP part, to reduce the number of parameters and the computational cost, we impose 4 × 4 sublattice structure for the 8 × 8, 12 × 12, and 16 × 16 lattices ... In the case of the 4 × 4 sublattice structure, the number of independent f_ij parameters is reduced from N_site^2 to 4 × 4 × N_site = 16 N_site ... Then, the number of relevant f_ij parameters is 16(N_site − 1). ... In the present study, we fix the number of hidden units N_hidden to be 16. ... For each J2 point, we perform at least three independent optimizations of the RBM+PP wave functions from different initial variational parameters. ... Sec. VI: In the actual calculations, we employ the sublattice structure in the f_ij parameters for the 8 × 8, 12 × 12, 16 × 16, and 18 × 18 lattices, to reduce the computational cost from O(N_site^4) to O(N_site^3) (see Appendix A). ... in the case of the 8 × 8 lattice at J2 = 0.5, the ground-state energy with the 4 × 4 sublattice structure is −0.498460(6), which is compared to −0.498886(1) obtained without a sublattice structure. ... Acknowledgments: The implementation of the RBM+PP scheme is done based on the mVMC package [65]. The computation was mainly done at Supercomputer Center, Institute for Solid State Physics, University of Tokyo, and RIKEN supercomputers K and Fugaku.

The quoted J2 = 0.5 value -0.498460(6) is explicitly the 4×4-sublattice run; the J2 = 0.55 value -0.48781 is not printed in the arXiv text (Table I lists the no-sublattice value -0.488820(2)) and is presumably the sublattice-structured phase-diagram run. No sample count, SR iteration count, wall-clock, core count or hours stated; at least three independent optimizations per J2; cost scaling O(N_site^3) with sublattice structure; computed on ISSP, K and Fugaku supercomputers (no quantities).
